summary: Break or exploit a cipher/protocol to recover a secret. Identify the primitive (RSA / AES / XOR / classical / ECC / hash / PRNG), then apply the matching attack. Most CTF crypto is a known textbook weakness, not novel cryptanalysis.
quick_triage: Read ALL provided files (source .py, params, ciphertext, public key). The vuln is almost always visible in the handrolled code.
Identify the primitive: openssl asn1parse / rsa -pubin -text for keys; `file` and entropy for blobs; look for n,e,c (RSA), iv/mode (AES), repeating-key patterns (XOR).
RSA: feed the public key to RsaCtfTool --attack all; check factordb for n.
Unknown number/bytes: CyberChef 'Magic', or try base64/hex/decimal decode chains first.
If an oracle/service is given (padding, LSB, length-extension), the attack is interactive — script it with pwntools/requests.

tools.name: python3 + pycryptodome
tools.when: Scripting every crypto attack; AES/RSA/hash primitives.
tools.usage: from Crypto.Util.number import long_to_bytes, inverse, GCD

tools.name: gmpy2
tools.when: Fast bignum math: iroot, gcd, invert for RSA attacks.

tools.name: sympy
tools.when: Factoring, discrete log (small), modular arithmetic, symbolic.

tools.name: RsaCtfTool
tools.when: RSA with weak/attackable params — the first thing to try on any RSA key.

tools.name: SageMath
tools.when: Heavy algebra: lattices (LLL/Coppersmith), ECC, DLP, polynomial rings. The crypto power tool.

install.note: large; use a sage docker image or cloud (cocalc) if the sandbox can't build it

tools.name: factordb (lookup)
tools.when: Any RSA modulus n — may already be factored in the public DB.
tools.usage: from factordb.factordb import FactorDB; f=FactorDB(n); f.connect(); f.get_factor_list()

tools.name: yafu
tools.when: Offline factoring of medium moduli (SIQS/ECM) when factordb misses.

tools.name: xortool
tools.when: Repeating-key XOR: recover key length and key.

tools.name: hashcat
tools.when: Crack password hashes / weak key derivations (GPU).

tools.name: john (John the Ripper)
tools.when: Crack hashes, and *2john converters for encrypted files/keys.

tools.name: hash-identifier / hashid
tools.when: Identify an unknown hash type before cracking.

tools.name: hashpumpy / hash_extender
tools.when: Hash length-extension attacks (MD5/SHA1/SHA2 MACs built as hash(secret||msg)).
tools.usage: import hashpumpy; hashpumpy.hashpump(sig, data, append, keylen)

tools.name: z3-solver
tools.when: Constraint solving: break custom/LCG PRNGs, linear cipher systems.

tools.name: randcrack / mersenne predictor
tools.when: Predict Python random / MT19937 after observing 624 outputs.

tools.name: openssl
tools.when: Parse keys/certs, quick enc/dec, inspect ASN.1.

tools.name: CyberChef (reference, offline build)
tools.when: Rapid decode/encoding-chain discovery, 'Magic' detector, classical ciphers.

install.note: web app; host the static build offline or use gchq.github.io/CyberChef

tools.usage: Magic / From Base64 / XOR Brute Force recipes

tools.name: FeatherDuster
tools.when: Automated, modular cryptanalysis — quick first pass to detect cipher/encoding and known weaknesses.

tools.name: rsatool
tools.when: Generate an RSA private key once you know p and q (or reconstruct d/n).

tools.name: padding-oracle-attacker
tools.when: Run a CBC padding-oracle attack from the CLI against a live oracle.

tools.name: PkCrack
tools.when: Break legacy ZipCrypto (pkzip) with a known-plaintext file from the archive.
tools.usage: pkcrack -C enc.zip -c file -P plain.zip -p file -d out.zip

tools.name: quipqiup
tools.when: Auto-solve substitution / Vigenere ciphers without a key.
